body:
sara_cs: Hey team — Medvera (customer) asked for evidence that embeddings generated from PHI are pseudonymized before storage. They want: short statement we can give legal, how long embeddings are retained, and whether raw prompts are stored. Need answer by EOD Fri.

emily_legal: @sara_cs thanks. We should provide a concise legal-friendly statement + attachments. Key points: (1) what we consider "pseudonymization" for embeddings, (2) whether re-identification is feasible with our pipeline, (3) retention windows and deletion proofs, (4) whether any raw PII persists. I can draft wording once engineering confirms practice.

mohit_se: Quick overview from infra side: for hosted Redwood API we do NOT persist plaintext prompts in long-term storage; request logs are ephemeral (30d rolling logs for debugging) unless customer opts into longer retention. Embeddings are stored encrypted at rest. For tenant-scoped metadata we store a tenant_id (opaque GUID). We perform a deterministic salt+hash on user identifiers before attaching them to embeddings metadata for internal indexing — that is our pseudonymization step.

sara_cs: Mohit — can you confirm if the deterministic salt is per-customer or global? Medvera cares about cross-tenant linkability.

mohit_se: It's per-customer salt in Dedicated and Private deployments (customer-managed KMS option too). For hosted we currently use a per-tenant salt generated at provisioning time and rotated quarterly. Rotation is documented but old salts are retained encrypted for lookup window (30 days).

emily_legal: That per-tenant salt answer should be prominent. Legal will likely ask for confirmation that salts are never stored with cleartext IDs and that KMS access is limited. Also add high-level SOC2 control references for crypto/key management. I'll draft a short paragraph.

jordan_cust: FYI Medvera's intake form also asked "can embeddings be returned to us deleted on demand?" — they want a deletion API or confirmation of purge.

mohit_se: We have a deletion path: for Dedicated/Private customers we can run targeted purge via the tenant tooling (and produce a purge runbook). For hosted customers we support deletion requests via our support flow and can provide proof of deletion (logs). It isn't a self-serve API today — that's a product request.

sara_cs: Noted. @rachel_pm can we flag self-serve deletion as a priority for roadmap? At least a docable process is needed for now.

rachel_pm: Yep — will add an entry to the roadmap backlog. For this request, we should deliver: 1) one-page legal statement, 2) one-page engineering playbook (pseudonymization + retention), 3) screenshots/export showing encryption settings + sample purge log. I can help assemble.

ops-bot: CS ticket CS-4928 created for Medvera evidence request (owner: sara_cs)

sara_cs: Emily — can you draft the legal statement? Mohit + Rachel, can you collaborate on the playbook and gather export screenshots? I’ll package and send to Medvera asking for confirmation.

emily_legal: Draft incoming in ~2 hours. Will include: suggested DPA addendum language, a brief explanation of pseudonymization we use (hash+salt, salt rotation, KMS), and recommended audit artifacts.

mohit_se: I'll pull the storage encryption screenshot and the salt rotation config (sanitized) — will redact any internal-only IDs. Expect artifacts by EOD today.

jordan_cust: Can we also include a short Q&A for Medvera's security reviewer? They often like an FAQ.

sara_cs: Good call — add a 5-item FAQ.

ops-bot: Reminder: EOD deadline Fri 2024-11-15 17:00 UTC added to CS-4928

sara_cs: Thanks all. I'll compile once docs are in and send to Medvera legal. If we can't meet EOD, call out exact ETA in thread. :thumbsup:

emily_legal: Uploaded draft to CS-4928. Quick note: do not promise self-serve deletion in legal statement — say "deletion on request with audit" unless product confirms API.

mohit_se: Artifacts uploaded to the ticket: storage-screenshot.png, salt-rotation-redacted.txt, purge-log-sample.txt.

sara_cs: Packaging now, will ping when sent.

jordan_cust: Appreciate the quick turn. Medvera legal will likely follow up with a short checklist.

sara_cs: Thread closed for now — will reopen if Medvera asks follow-ups.
